text:
**My pick: the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 ($899).** It's the only specific model the results recommend by name. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop) lists it at 2,073.6 Wh (LiFePO4) with a 2,600 W AC inverter, and says it was in stock on 2026-11-04. That inverter handles an 1,800 W induction plate with headroom. Dealectric also says boiling a litre of water takes only about 90–110 Wh, so one charge covers many boils or meals. [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). Dealectric sells this unit, so treat its recommendation with that in mind. I only have its numbers, not independent testing.

**What matters when you choose**
- **Inverter watts matter most.** A single-burner portable induction cooktop (such as the Duxtop 9100MC) draws up to 1,800 W. [HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/) says to look for at least 1,800 W continuous and 1,800 W surge. Small units like the EcoFlow RIVER 3 (300 W) and RIVER 3 Plus (600 W) can't run it, no matter how big the battery is. [BlackoutWise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/induction-cooktop) says the same about the 300 Wh class and the Goal Zero Yeti 500.
- **The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 is borderline.** BlackoutWise says it stops at 1,500 W, so it would need a lower power setting.
- **The smallest unit that can run one at full power** is the DJI Power 1000, according to HomePowerFacts. But it would only last about 0.4 h at 1,800 W.
- **Capacity sets how long you can cook.** BlackoutWise says a burner on high averages about 1,080 W as it cycles. That gives roughly 45–50 minutes on a 1,000 Wh unit and about 3 hours on the 4,096 Wh EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3. [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/devices/induction-cooktop) says a 2,000 Wh-class station gives about an hour at a full 1,800 W. It also says a 20-minute meal at mixed power levels typically uses 300–500 Wh.

**Tips**
- Boil at high power, then drop to 400–800 W to simmer. PowerStationMatch says this can halve the battery used.
- A station running near its limit gets hot and may cut output. [VanLifeKitchens](https://vanlifekitchens.com/guides/can-a-power-station-run-an-induction-cooktop) advises keeping the vents clear.

**Electric kettle:** the results don't give kettle wattage. Most kettles draw about as much as an induction burner, so the same inverter check applies. The Elite 200 V2's 2,600 W inverter should cover one, but I'm inferring that and the results don't confirm it.

**If you need more power or runtime:** a bigger unit like the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh) gives the longest runtime among the models mentioned. Its price wasn't in the results. For a quick kettle or one meal, the Elite 200 V2 is enough.
